text:
priya: flagging a canary issue: after a prefix handoff we observed occasional stale reads where the receiver had acknowledged ownership but hadn't applied the demote tombstone yet. reproducible with a tiny race under CPU pressure.

priya: minimal repro notes:
1) prefix P owned by node-A epoch=101
2) node-A initiates handoff -> node-B, router updates ownership quickly
3) node-B acks but apply of demote/tombstone is queued and delayed
4) router sends read to node-B; node-B serves pre-demote snapshot -> stale value returned

sam: thanks. sounds like the root is that ownership becomes visible before apply completes. Options: a) router waits synchronously for receiver to commit (latency cost), b) receiver exposes durable applied marker and router falls back until it's set (cheap reads), c) change handoff so receiver applies before claiming ownership (bigger refactor).

leo: leaning to (b). make receiver write a tiny durable marker for applied_epoch. API: `POST /prefix/:p/apply {epoch, nonce, tombstone}` -> `{applied_epoch, already}`. On commit we fsync a small manifest {prefix->applied_epoch}. Router caches applied_epoch per node. If unknown or < epoch, route to fallback.

nora: agree. also include idempotency: server records nonce per-prefix for recent window to avoid double-apply. nonce storage can be an LRU persisted as part of manifest. Edge: restarts must restore last_applied_epoch, so manifest is authoritative.

priya: tradeoffs: one fsync per handoff commit, but handoffs are infrequent. we pay reliability for correctness. Also need a timeout/drain-window: if apply stalls beyond X seconds, router should continue routing to fallback and surface alert. we should avoid blocking global operations.

sam: router behaviour detail: when cluster state shows new owner for prefix with epoch E, router async fetches nodeB.applied_epoch. If cached value >= E then route. If unknown or < E, route to fallback owner or proxy. Additionally, include header `X-ownership-pending` so downstream clients can optionally retry.

leo: implementation sketch on receiver:
```
lock(prefix)
if epoch <= last_applied_epoch: return already
if nonce seen: return already
persist manifest {last_applied_epoch=epoch, seen_nonces+=nonce} (fsync)
apply tombstone in-memory async
unlock
return applied_epoch=epoch
```
This ensures monotonicity and crash-safety.

nora: monitoring: `apply.commit_ms` (p50/p95), `apply.nonce_conflicts`, `apply.stalled` (count of applies > threshold), and `router.applied_epoch_misses`. Alert p95 commit > 2s in canary.

priya: test plan: unit idempotency, integration restart replay, chaos test with heavy GC/CPU to force delayed applies, and load test to verify router fallback doesn't overload old owner.

sam: rollout: feature-flag `prefix_apply_marker`. Steps: canary1 -> canary10 -> canary50 -> prod. Backwards compatibility: if receiver doesn't support marker, router uses opaque-token fallback.

leo: one more thing: batch fsync optimization: if a node receives many apply requests in short window, group manifests and fsync once, but ensure per-prefix visibility only after fsync includes that prefix. We can use a per-node commit barrier that marks all included prefixes as applied atomically. Complexity moderate, maybe in follow-up.

nora: I'll add dashboard panels and set up chaos job. priya, can you open a short RFC with API shape and manifest format? I'll pair on metrics.

infra-bot: action items created: RFC (#4523), chaos job (#4524), feature-flag `prefix_apply_marker` toggles, metrics to add. Recommended rollout: canary -> staged -> prod.

priya: thanks all. the marker approach seems lowest-risk and will close the canary repro without reworking the whole handoff flow. sync Thursday 9am to review RFC. :thumbsup:
